simple.meaning: גָּדַר (gâdar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to wall in or around.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 10 times in 2 Kings, Job, Isaiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, and 2 more, beginning at 2 Kings 12:13. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּדַר (H1443) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּדַר (gâdar) / H1443 is traced through 2 Kings 12:13, 2 Kings 22:6, Job 19:8, Isaiah 58:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1443. gadar גָּדַר verb wall up or off, build a wall (denominative? Late Hebrew id. , Arabic and see גָּדֵר below) — Qal Perfect גָּדַר Job 19:8 2 t., וְגָדַרְתִּ֫י Hosea 2:8 ; Amos 9:11 ; Imperfect 2masculine plural וַתִּגְדְּרוּ Ezek 13:5 ; Participle גֹּדֵר Isa 58:12 ; Ezek 22:30 ; plural גֹּדְרִים 2Kin 12:13 ; 22:6 ; — wall up, shut off , literal only Participle , absolute = masons (wall-builders) 12:13 ; 22:6 ; also Isa 58:12 (object מֶּרֶץ ); figurative of Yahweh's dealings with men, object אֹרַה Job 19:8 , דֶּרֶך Lam 3:9 ; compare Hosea 2:8 (accusative of congnate meaning with verb גָּדֵר ), in all = obstructing path of life, compare also Lam 3:7 (with בַּעֲדִי ); of restoring fallen booth of David Amos 9:11 (object פרצים ); of repairing fortunes of Israel, a work neglected by prophets Ezek 13:5 , and by all in power 22:30 (both with accusative of congnate meaning with verb)
